seeds.bootstrap_derivation: Each comparison's bootstrap seed is pulsegraph.random.derived_seed(20260917, component, comparison id, domain, model, reference, horizon, metric): the first four bytes, read as a little-endian unsigned 32-bit integer, of the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of json.dumps([20260917, component, comparison id, domain, model, reference, horizon, metric], sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) with Python's default separators ', ' and ': ' and ASCII escaping; the root and the horizon are integers, every other field a string. The generator is numpy.random.default_rng(seed). A secondary contrast reuses a family row's model and reference with its own horizon and metric in the same derivation; its id is the family id, or the family id with '-h7' for a horizon outside the family.
seeds.pit_derivation: Each saved forecast with a count law per target day draws its uniforms from numpy.random.default_rng(pulsegraph.random.derived_seed(20260916, component, domain, series_id, cutoff, horizon, model)), the same SHA-256 derivation with the cutoff as the run's string label; V = rng.random(horizon), one uniform per target day in lead order. U = F(y-) + V (F(y) - F(y-)) with F(y-) = 1 - SF(y - 1) and F(y) = 1 - SF(y) of the saved law. Ten equal bins on [0, 1], the last closed. Raw native deciles, local_mean_28 and autoets_weekly have no full count law, and their PIT is unavailable.
